extension.description: A shared visual canvas for managing parallel AI agent and terminal sessions in VS Code. Orchestrate multi-agent workflows on one workbench.
capabilities.untrusted.description: Open the canvas and inspect saved layouts in untrusted workspaces. Execution entry points such as Agent and Terminal are disabled until the workspace is trusted.
capabilities.virtual.description: This version requires a Node.js workspace extension host, host shell, and local filesystem workspace. Virtual workspaces are not supported.

configuration.title: Dev Session Canvas
configuration.canvas.defaultSurface.desc: The host surface where the main canvas appears by default. The default is `panel`; VS Code remembers the actual workbench position of that view, so users can move it. When set to `panel`, VS Code can show the native Panel entry before the extension or canvas activates, but the extension will not force the canvas to the foreground. After the canvas is activated in the current window, that window keeps using the already-applied surface. Changing this setting requires Window Reload to fully switch the default surface.
configuration.canvas.overviewMode.descri: Controls whether the canvas switches to a lower-information overview rendering after it zooms below the overview threshold. The threshold is controlled by `devSessionCanvas.canvas.overviewZoomThreshold`. This setting does not affect dynamic minimum zoom or whether fit view can zoom below `0.4`.
configuration.canvas.overviewMode.none.d: Keep normal node rendering at every zoom level and never enter overview mode.
Show node titles inside node content areas after the canvas reaches overview zoom, making nodes easier to identify quickly.
configuration.canvas.overviewZoomThresho: Zoom threshold for overview mode. Values range from `0` to `1`; the default is `0.2`. When canvas zoom is below this value and overview mode is not `none`, overview rendering is enabled. Changes apply to the current canvas and do not affect dynamic minimum zoom or fit view.
configuration.canvas.multiRootPresentati: Controls how multi-root workspaces are presented on the canvas. The default `rootGroups` keeps the existing single composed canvas and system root groups. `paneGallery` shows each workspace root as an interactive pane and provides dynamic, grid, top-thumbnail, and side-thumbnail local modes in the lower-left canvas controls. This setting only affects multi-root workspaces; single-root workspaces continue to show a single-root canvas.
Use the existing single composed canvas, with each workspace root shown as a system root group.
Show each workspace root as an interactive pane with dynamic, grid, top-thumbnail, and side-thumbnail local modes.
configuration.canvas.linkOpenMode.descri: Controls how clickable external links inside the canvas are opened. By default, `http` and `https` links open in VS Code's built-in Simple Browser in the editor, preserving workbench context; remote localhost and loopback links are resolved through VS Code port forwarding first. When external browser mode is selected, external links open with the system default browser or app. Workspace file links still open in the VS Code editor.
configuration.canvas.linkOpenMode.editor: Open `http` and `https` links in VS Code's built-in Simple Browser in the editor. Remote localhost and loopback links are resolved through VS Code port forwarding first. Other safe external schemes continue through the VS Code opener.
configuration.canvas.linkOpenMode.extern: Open external links with the system default browser or app. Remote localhost links still use VS Code's external opener so port forwarding can be handled.
configuration.canvas.workspaceRootWaterm: Controls whether system root section bodies in multi-root workspaces show tiled root-name watermarks. Enabled by default. When disabled, root section titles and full-path tooltips remain available.
configuration.runtimePersistence.enabled: When enabled, Agent and Terminal sessions are preferably owned by the independent runtime host backend. Local Linux and Remote SSH provide strong guarantees when `systemd --user` is available; otherwise the extension falls back to a detached supervisor and marks it as best-effort in logs and diagnostics. Changes require Window Reload to take effect. Switching this setting clears the current workspace canvas host state on the next load.
configuration.agent.defaultProvider.desc: Default CLI provider used when creating new Agent nodes.
configuration.agent.codexCommand.descrip: Command name or absolute path used to start the Codex CLI. By default, it is resolved from the Extension Host `PATH`.
configuration.agent.claudeCommand.descri: Command name or absolute path used to start the Claude Code CLI. By default, it is resolved from the Extension Host `PATH`.
configuration.agent.codexDefaultArgs.des: Default argument fragment appended when creating a Codex Agent or starting a new Codex session. Enter stable arguments only: do not repeat the command itself, and do not include one-off session targets such as resume/fork, `--last`, `--all`, `--include-non-interactive`, or bare positional prompts/session IDs that conflict with Resume/Fork placement. Uses window scope, so it can be overridden for the current window or workspace.
configuration.agent.claudeDefaultArgs.de: Default argument fragment appended when creating a Claude Code Agent or starting a new Claude session. Enter stable arguments only: do not repeat the command itself, and do not include one-off session targets such as `--resume`/`-r`, `--continue`/`-c`, `--session-id`, or `--fork-session` that conflict with Resume/Fork placement. Uses window scope, so it can be overridden for the current window or workspace.
configuration.notifications.attentionSig: Where execution-node attention should be bridged in addition to the canvas. Regardless of this setting, generated node attention icons and same-color brightness flashing in the minimap remain enabled.
Do not show additional workbench messages or system notifications. Keep only node attention surfaces and diagnostic events.
Bridge attention signals to VS Code workbench messages using `vscode.window.showInformationMessage`.

Prefer sending attention signals to the local UI-side `Dev Session Canvas Notifier` companion. If the companion is unavailable or delivery fails, automatically fall back to a VS Code workbench message.
configuration.notifications.enabledAtten: Controls which attention signals can generate Dev Session Canvas attention. Disabled signals do not set node attention, flash the minimap, or bridge to workbench/system notifications. By default, `bel`, `osc9`, `osc777`, `agentAbnormalExit`, and `codexAbnormalOutputText` are enabled. Set this to an empty array to disable all attention.
configuration.notifications.strongTermin: After an execution node enters attention, the node attention icon and same-color brightness flashing in the minimap always remain. This option only controls additional strong reminder surfaces. Values are `none`, `titleBar`, `minimap`, and `both`; the default is `both`.
Do not enable additional strong reminders. Keep only the node attention icon and same-color minimap flashing.
Only flash the execution node title bar. Do not add a size pulse to the minimap.
Only add a size pulse to the corresponding minimap node in addition to same-color brightness flashing. Do not flash the title bar.
Enable both title-bar flashing and minimap size pulse.
configuration.notifications.agentAbnorma: Whether known abnormal text in Agent terminal output should trigger additional reminders. This feature is disabled by default. When enabled, it only supplements provider-native notifications and does not automatically recover the provider or replay prompts.
Do not trigger additional abnormal-text reminders from terminal output. Abnormal interruption reminders for already-running Agents that exit non-zero without a user stop are still kept.

Trigger supplemental reminders only for high-confidence final Codex failure text. Current matches include the square-marker `■ {"error":{"message":"Internal server error"}}` and the tail output `■ stream disconnected before completion: stream closed before response.completed`. Tree-indented stream-disconnected lines under `Reconnecting... n/m` are retry/reconnect transient output and do not trigger reminders. Claude Code text matching is not enabled until structured StopFailure data or real output samples are available.
configuration.terminal.shell.description: Select the shell type used by embedded Terminal nodes. This setting supports a current-device default and workspace overrides. Once either Terminal shell setting is explicitly assigned at workspace scope, the workspace-level `terminal.shell` and `terminal.shellPath` are used together, without mixing in the other half from device scope. The extension dynamically resolves the selected shell type to an available shell path on the current device and shows a prompt if it is unavailable. If `terminal.shellPath` is also set, that exact path always takes precedence. To choose and lock one concrete copy discovered on the current device, use the `Dev Session Canvas: Select Terminal Shell` command. When opened in a workspace, that command writes a workspace override by default.
configuration.terminal.shell.default.des: Follow the host default shell. Prefer VS Code's currently detected default shell; if missing, fall back to `SHELL` on Linux/macOS and `COMSPEC` on Windows.
configuration.terminal.shell.bash.descri: Dynamically resolve the actual available `bash` path on the current device and use it to start embedded Terminal nodes.
configuration.terminal.shell.zsh.descrip: Dynamically resolve the actual available `zsh` path on the current device and use it to start embedded Terminal nodes.
configuration.terminal.shell.fish.descri: Dynamically resolve the actual available `fish` path on the current device and use it to start embedded Terminal nodes.
configuration.terminal.shell.sh.descript: Dynamically resolve the actual available `sh` path on the current device and use it to start embedded Terminal nodes.
configuration.terminal.shell.pwsh.descri: Dynamically resolve the actual available `pwsh` path on the current device and use it to start embedded Terminal nodes.
Dynamically resolve the actual available `powershell` path on the current device and use it to start embedded Terminal nodes.
configuration.terminal.shell.cmd.descrip: Dynamically resolve the actual available `cmd` path on the current device and use it to start embedded Terminal nodes.
configuration.terminal.shellPath.descrip: Explicitly specify the exact command path used to start embedded Terminal node shells. This setting supports a current-device default and workspace overrides. Once either Terminal shell setting is explicitly assigned at workspace scope, the workspace-level `terminal.shell` and `terminal.shellPath` are used together, without mixing in the other half from device scope. The `Dev Session Canvas: Select Terminal Shell` command dynamically detects shells available on the current device and writes the selected path here. Even when multiple shells share the same name, the recorded path is preferred. When opened in a workspace, that command writes a workspace override by default; to change the device-level default, edit User Settings directly. If this path is unavailable on the current device, the extension shows a prompt. Leave empty to dynamically resolve the actual shell from the `terminal.shell` setting.
configuration.terminal.inheritEnv.descri: Controls whether embedded Terminal nodes inherit the controlled environment delta resolved from the current shell. Enabled by default. On macOS/Linux this fills in PATH, Homebrew, NVM, or toolchain variables that can be missing when VS Code is launched from a GUI. Windows Terminal always lets the real shell run its own profile or AutoRun; this setting does not pre-apply a shell env patch for Windows Terminal. If you see duplicated PATH entries or profile side effects, disable this setting or adjust `devSessionCanvas.terminal.shellArgs`.
configuration.terminal.shellArgs.descrip: Additional argv entries passed when starting the embedded Terminal shell, equivalent to the args part of a Terminal profile. The default empty array preserves the existing launch shape. You can set `["-l"]`, `["--login"]`, or other arguments supported by the current shell. This setting only affects Terminal nodes and does not affect structured Agent provider CLI launch arguments.
configuration.files.enabled.description: Whether Agent file activity is enabled. Disabled by default. When disabled, file nodes, file-list nodes, file filtering, and automatic file relations are turned off, and file activity/filtering state is cleared on the next load. Changes require Window Reload to take effect.
configuration.files.presentationMode.des: Default presentation mode for Agent file activity. The default is `lists`. `nodes` shows files as independent nodes; `lists` consolidates them into file-list nodes by Agent and shared relationships.
configuration.fileNode.displayStyle.desc: Display style for file nodes and file-list nodes. `card` keeps the current card style; `minimal` uses a more compact style closer to VS Code's native file list.
configuration.files.nodeDisplayMode.desc: Display mode for file nodes. By default, both icon and path are shown.
configuration.files.pathDisplayMode.desc: How paths are displayed for file nodes and file-list entries. By default, only the file name is shown.
configuration.noteMarkdown.stripExtensio: When a Markdown file is dropped onto empty canvas space to create a linked Note, controls whether the `.md` or `.markdown` suffix is stripped from the default Note title. Disabled by default, so the title keeps the full file name.
